20. The hot water bag is used to give hot pressure to the parts of a body. Why?
Ans:- A hot water bag is used to give hot pressure to body parts because the heat from the bag transfers to the body,
improving blood circulation and relieving pain or stiffness.
21. Touching a cup of hot tea feels hot but touching an ice cube feels cool. Explain it based on the motion of their molecules.
Ans:- Touching a hot cup of tea feels hot because its molecules move very fast, having high kinetic energy, which transfers
heat to our hand. Touching an ice cube feels cool because its molecules move very slowly, having low kinetic energy, so heat
from our hand flows into the ice.
22. If the lid of a glass bottle does not open, how may it be opened using your knowledge of the effects of heat? Explained on
Ans:- The lid of a glass bottle can be opened by warming the neck of the bottle under hot water. Heating increases the kinetic
energy of the air molecules inside, causing them to expand and exert pressure on the lid, making it easier to open.
23. Once in winter, while drinking the water from a steel glass on the table. Samir felt the water to be warmer towards the
bottom. Justify his experience based on scientific facts.
Ans:- Samir felt the water warmer at the bottom because heat from the surrounding air is lost more quickly from the top
surface, while the bottom retains more heat due to less exposure to cold and the thermal conductivity of the steel glass, so the
temperature at the bottom is slightly higher.

28. In the perception of a certain man, a bucket of lukewarm water contains more thermal energy than a large tank of cold
water. Correct this understanding based on the definitions of thermal energy and temperature.
Ans:- The man’s understanding is incorrect because thermal energy depends on both the mass of the substance and the
temperature, not just how warm it feels. A large tank of cold water contains far more molecules than a small bucket, so even
at a lower temperature, it has more total thermal energy than the lukewarm water in the bucket.
